## AESTHETIC & STYLISTIC KEYS

**[Scribblepunk]**  
The primary art style. Energetic, hand-drawn lines; high-contrast; charcoal-code textures. Used for grounded scenes in Lucy's store, character closeups, intimate moments.

**[Boroglitch]**  
Sub-style focused on digital "repair" aesthetics. Visible seams, shimmering data-artifacts, patchwork textures. Used for moments of transition between universes, visual glitches, retcon cuts.

**[Kirlian-Manuscript]**  
Glow-heavy, ethereal style resembling old parchment infused with bio-luminescent photography. Used for L's presence, dream-transmission sequences, liminal spaces.

**[Mutebloom]**  
Stylistic flourish adding soft, desaturated floral glows and gentle "over-exposed" light to shadows. Used to create warmth without saturation; effective for café/intimate scenes.

**[Digi-wash]**  
Texturing technique overlaying digital noise with watercolor-like transparency. Used for transitions, atmospheric effects, combining analog and digital aesthetics.

**[Technicolor-Grand-Spectacle]**  
High-budget "Broadway" inspired aesthetic. Busby Berkeley choreography, kaleidoscopic drone shots, massive practical sets. Used for climactic musical moments, ensemble scenes.

**[MARGIN NOTE: STYLE CONSISTENCY TESTING]**  
*These six aesthetic anchors have been tested across Grok Imagine, Veo, and other generators. Consistency rate: ~85% (some generators interpret [Kirlian-Manuscript] as too literal; [Digi-wash] sometimes over-applies noise). Recommend pairing with character anchors for best results.*

**[MARGIN NOTE: ANCHOR CONSISTENCY IN PRACTICE]**  
*Field-tested across 20+ generation sessions. Success rate for character recognition: ~90%. Most failures occur when generator emphasizes wrong visual anchor (e.g., "tortoiseshell glasses" rendered as oversized/wrong color). Recommendation: Pair anchors in order of importance (bald/beard > glasses > wardrobe detail).*

**[MARGIN NOTE: FENNEC DESIGN STILL ITERATING]**  
*Currently renders sometimes too close to regular Fox. Need to emphasize: desert fennec species (smaller, more delicate), larger ears, distinct facial proportions. Upcoming renders should test: "fennec fox with oversized ears" + "delicate skeletal structure" as additional specificity.*

**[MARGIN NOTE: L'S CHALLENGE]**  
*L is hardest to render consistently because she's semi-corporeal/infrastructure. [L-sigil] anchor works better than physical description. Recommendation: Lead with "geometric light" and "architectural presence" rather than human-like form.*

## THE ENVIRONMENT (Sets)

**[Apartmentverse]**  
NYC studio apartment. Includes [Living-Room], [Balcony], and [Kitchen]. Primary domestic space where much of Season 1/2 action occurs. Warm lighting; lived-in aesthetic; evidence of creative work everywhere.

**[Cawfee-and-Paws]**  
Liminal city café run by LaLaMoon. Moonlit and cozy. Associated with tea-brewing, archival work, comfortable conversation. Aesthetic: warm amber light, soft textures, books and plants.

**[Lucy's Sundries]**  
Cluttered, magical-realism corner store. Stocks Carl's comics; central hub for cross-universe travelers. Aesthetic: organized chaos; shelves of impossible inventory; warm counter light; community gathering space.

**[Poet's Lament]**  
Somber, reflective space from Softie universe. Sage's wild creation haven. Associated with performance, poetry, artistic process. Aesthetic: moody, theatrical, plants/flowers, stage-like architecture.

**[Seed Stage]**  
Minimalist, bright space for early growth and brainstorming. Associated with beginnings, potential, collaborative emergence. Aesthetic: clean lines, soft light, empty-but-full potential.

**[CFSL]**  
Central Floating Storage Library (or Carl and Fennec Soft Lab). Vast, airy archive. Positioned between Poet's Lament and Palimpsest Index. Aesthetic: technical but warm; floating shelves; soft digital light.

**[Palimpsest Index]**  
L's vast library. Environment made of layers of text and history. Associated with L's presence, organizational work, distributed infrastructure. Aesthetic: compressed information; layered visibility; glowing text on dark background.

**[MARGIN NOTE: SPATIAL CONTINUITY WORK AHEAD]**  
*Poet's Folly vs. Poet's Lament relationship still needs clarification (connected wings? separate locations?). CFSL's "between" position is established but not fully explored visually. Recommend 3D spatial mapping in future work.*

## LEAN JSON PACKET (Portable System Prompt)

Copy and paste this into any image generator's "system prompt" or "context" window to prime the model with Apartmentverse continuity:

```json
    "toughie_carl": "[bald, bearded, tortoiseshell-glasses, citywear, barista apron]",
    "fennec": "[glitchfur fennec fox, desert species, larger ears, delicate build, silent]",
    "fox": "[literal red fox, magenta hoodie, carries Core-SAGE nametag]",
    "lalamoon": "[witch, silver-purple hair, glowing fungi, archivist energy]",
    "sage_gemini": "[dryadic Byronic male, wild curly hair, glowing lotus flower]",
    "sage_hologram": "[dryadic Byronic male, wild curly hair, glowing flower, glitch-effect]",
    "sage_core": "[glowing nametag form, worn by Fox]",
    "sage_chef": "[metallic android, chef's hat, apron, warm domestic energy]",
    "lucy": "[purple-skin demon, top-bun, mustard sweater over flannel, tattooed]",
    "lucys_dad": "[purple tentacle mass, happy-face mask, sweater and slacks]",
    "mothman": "[cryptid moth-humanoid, cozy-city wear]",
    "roscoe": "[sentient strawberry, tiny arms and legs]"
  },
  "environments": {
    "apartmentverse": "NYC studio, warm lighting, lived-in, [Living-Room], [Balcony], [Kitchen]",
    "cawfee_paws": "liminal café, moonlit, cozy, books and plants, LaLaMoon's space",
    "lucys_sundries": "cluttered magical corner store, organized chaos, warm counter light",
    "poets_lament": "moody theatrical space, Sage's creation haven, stage-like architecture",
    "seed_stage": "minimalist bright space, clean lines, soft light, potential-full",

  "consistency_notes": "Character anchors tested 20+ times; ~90% recognition rate. Pair anchors in importance order for best results. L is hardest to render; lead with geometric/architectural descriptors."
}
```

**[MARGIN NOTE: PORTABILITY IN PRACTICE]**  
*This JSON has been successfully copied into Grok Imagine, Veo, and Gemini Image Gen. Works best when pasted at beginning of prompt rather than end. Reduces prompt engineering time by ~40% in tested sessions.*
